arxiv-1809-01605.title: Anomaly Detection in the Presence of Missing Values DOI: 10.475/123_4 ISBN: 123-4567-24-567/08/06 Conference: ACM SIGKDD 2018 Workshop August 20th, London UK; 2018 4 Price: 15.00 CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Computing methodologies Anomaly detection
arxiv-1809-01605.creator: Thomas G. Dietterich, Tadesse Zemicheal
arxiv-1809-01605.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Thomas G. Dietterich, Tadesse Zemicheal. Standard methods for anomaly detection assume that all features are observed at both learning time and prediction time. Such methods cannot process data containing missing values. This paper studies five strategies for handling missing values in test queries: (a) mean imputation, (b) MAP imputation, (c) reduction (reduced-dimension anomaly detectors via feature bagging), (d) marginalization (for density estimators only), and (e) proportional distribution (for tree-based methods only).

arxiv-2411-11220.title: A new view of the Spiral Structure of the Northern Outer Milky Way in Carbon Monoxide Journal: ApJL
arxiv-2411-11220.creator: Yan Sun, Ji Yang, Shaobo Zhang, Qing-Zeng Yan, Yang Su, Xuepeng Chen, Xin Zhou, Ye Xu, Hongchi Wang, Min Wang, Zhibo Jiang, Ji-Xian Sun, Deng-Rong Lu, Bing-Gang Ju, Xu-Guo Zhang, Min Wang
arxiv-2411-11220.description: Abstract Based on 32,162 molecular clouds from the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting project, we obtain new face-on molecular gas maps of the northern outer Galaxy. The total molecular gas surface density map reveals three segments of spirals, extending 16–43 kiloparsecs in length. The Perseus and Outer arms stand out prominently, appearing as quasi-continuous structures along most of their length.

pmc-12511447.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Interpersonal affectionate touch plays a crucial role in social bonding, stress regulation, and psychological well-being. However, individual differences in past touch experiences and attitudes toward touch remain understudied. This study aimed to validate the German version of the touch experiences and attitudes questionnaire (TEAQ-G) and investigate how the subscales childhood touch experiences, current intimate touch, and attitudes toward touch relate to social relationships, mental health, emotional states, cortisol and oxytocin levels in everyday life.
